title: Rope Cut – Free Rope-Cutting Physics Puzzle
description: Play Rope Cut free in your browser: swipe to cut the ropes, swing the candy into the jelly monster's mouth and grab 3 stars in 40 physics puzzles.
body: A candy dangles from a few ropes and a round green jelly monster is waiting below with its mouth wide open. Swipe across a rope to cut it, let the candy swing, and cut the next one at just the right moment so it drops into the monster's mouth.

There are 40 short levels in four colourful candy boxes, each with three stars to collect on the way. New ideas arrive one at a time: spike bars, soap bubbles that float the candy up, air puffers, pegs that grab it with a new rope, moving anchors and wind. Losing the candy costs nothing: the level resets in under a second. It works with a mouse or one finger, in landscape or portrait, and your stars, coins and the monster's hats are saved.
New here? Read how to play and the tips for three stars.

title: How to Play Rope Cut – Cutting, Bubbles, Puffers and Stars
description: Rope Cut controls: swipe across a rope to cut it, tap the bubble to pop it, tap a puffer to blow. Learn every object and how stars and coins work.
body: Goal: get the candy into the jelly monster's mouth. If it touches the monster's mouth, the monster eats it and the level is done.

Cut: press and drag across a rope (with the mouse or your finger) to cut it. You can cut several ropes with one long swipe, but usually the order matters: cut one, let the candy swing, then cut the next at the right moment.
Stars: each level has three stars. The candy collects a star by passing through it. Feeding the monster with all three stars gives the best score; any finish unlocks the next level.

Spike bars break the candy if it touches them. Bubbles catch the candy and float it upwards: tap the bubble to pop it and let the candy fall. Air puffers (the blue round pumps) blow a gust when you tap them and push the candy, or the bubble carrying it, away from their nozzle.

Pegs with a dotted circle throw out a new rope as soon as the candy flies into the circle. Moving anchors slide back and forth, so the moment you cut changes where the candy goes. Wind bands push anything that passes through them in the direction of the streaks.

Lost the candy? It crumbles or falls out of the box and the level starts again straight away. The round arrow button restarts at any time, and the grid button opens the level select. Every finished level pays coins (more with more stars) to spend in the shop on candy skins and hats for the monster.

title: Rope Cut Tips: How to Get Three Stars in Every Level
description: Practical tips for Rope Cut: timing your cuts on a swing, using bubbles and air puffers, pegs, moving anchors and wind to collect all three stars.
body: Watch the first swing before you cut again. After the first cut the candy swings on the remaining rope. Let it swing once and notice where the stars are on its path; then cut when it is moving towards the next star or the monster.
Cut near the top of the swing for a short drop, near the bottom for a long throw. At the bottom of a swing the candy is fastest, so it flies further when released.

The middle rope often does nothing on its own. When three or four ropes hold the candy, cutting a rope that is not under tension changes nothing, so start with the one that makes the candy swing towards the stars.
Bubbles rise slowly. There is plenty of time to wait for the candy to float past a high star before you pop the bubble. Pop it right above the monster.
Puffers push hardest up close. Tap the puffer when the candy is level with its nozzle. A bubble with a candy inside keeps drifting after the puff, so pop it a little before it is over the monster.
Pegs catch, then swing. Once a peg grabs the candy, it swings around the peg on a short rope. Cut that new rope when the candy is heading where you want it.
Moving anchors repeat. Watch one full slide and cut at the same spot next time.
Stuck? On some portals a video button appears after a few lost candies that skips to the next level. It is always optional, and you can come back later for the stars.

title: Rope Cut FAQ
description: Answers about Rope Cut: is it free, does it save, does it work on phones and Chromebooks, how many levels, how stars and coins work, how to skip a level.
body: Is it free? Yes, it is free to play in the browser, with no download and no sign-up.
How many levels are there? 40 short levels in four candy boxes of ten. Each one takes a few seconds once you know the trick.
Is every level possible with three stars? Yes. Every level is checked automatically by a bot that plays the real game physics and finds a three-star solution.
Does it save my progress? Yes. Unlocked levels, stars, coins and cosmetics are stored in your browser (or in your account on portals that offer it).
Does it work on phones and Chromebooks? Yes. It plays with one finger or a mouse, in portrait or landscape.

What are the coins for? Every level you finish pays coins, more for more stars, plus a daily gift. Spend them in the shop on new candy skins and hats for the monster. There are no real-money purchases.
Can I skip a level? On some game portals, after a few lost candies, a video button appears that skips to the next level. It is always optional.
Can I turn the music off? Yes, with the speaker button.

title: Rope Cut for Schools and Kids – Physics Puzzles, No Sign-up
description: Rope Cut is a short, text-free physics puzzle that runs on school Chromebooks: no chat, no purchases, no account, a playful way to explore swings and gravity.
h1: Rope Cut for classrooms and kids
body: Rope Cut has no chat, no account, no real-money purchases and no personal data. There is no text to read, only numbers and icons, so it works in any language and for early readers. Levels last a few seconds and can be stopped at any moment.
It runs in the browser on Chromebooks, tablets and computers with a mouse or a finger, and it is light (well under 1 MB plus music).

Every swing is simulated with real physics, so it is a playful way to talk about gravity, pendulums and momentum: why does the candy fly further when the rope is cut at the bottom of the swing? What does a gust of air do to a moving object? Ask students to predict where the candy will land before they cut.

It also practises planning and sequencing (which rope first?), timing and trial and error: a lost candy costs nothing and the level restarts instantly. There is no violence, only a happy monster and a crumbling candy.
Read how to play for the controls.
